review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

4:1.sourceText: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ ὁ δέσμιος ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀξίως περιπατῆσαι τῆς κλήσεως ἧς ἐκλήθητε,
4:1.targetText: I, the prisoner of the LORD, then call on you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,

groups.note: N1904 has the prepositional relation in the Lord, ἐν Κυρίῳ; LSV describes the same prisoner/Lord relation as of the LORD. This contextual noun-phrase rendering does not assert that ἐν generally means of.
The genitive relative ἧς relates to calling, rendered with which in the cognate called-with-a-calling construction; with belongs to that English complement relation.

4:2.sourceText: μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ πραΰτητος, μετὰ μακροθυμίας, ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων ἐν ἀγάπῃ,
4:2.targetText: with all lowliness and meekness, with long-suffering, bearing with one another in love,

4:3.sourceText: σπουδάζοντες τηρεῖν τὴν ἑνότητα τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐν τῷ συνδέσμῳ τῆς εἰρήνης·
4:3.targetText: being diligent to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace;

4:4.sourceText: ἓν σῶμα καὶ ἓν Πνεῦμα, καθὼς καὶ ἐκλήθητε ἐν μιᾷ ἐλπίδι τῆς κλήσεως ὑμῶν·
4:4.targetText: one body and one Spirit, according as you were also called in one hope of your calling;

4:5.sourceText: εἷς Κύριος, μία πίστις, ἓν βάπτισμα·
4:5.targetText: one Lord, one faith, one immersion,

4:6.sourceText: εἷς Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ πάντων, ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων καὶ διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν.
4:6.targetText: one God and Father of all, who [is] over all, and through all, and in you all,

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies the article-plus-prepositional modifier who is over all; Greek has no finite copula or being participle in this clause.
Source-witness pronoun addition: LSV in you all follows additional TR ὑμῖν; pinned N1904 has ἐν πᾶσιν without a you pronoun.

4:7.sourceText: Ἑνὶ δὲ ἑκάστῳ ἡμῶν ἐδόθη ἡ χάρις κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τῆς δωρεᾶς τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
4:7.targetText: and to each one of you was given grace, according to the measure of the gift of Christ,

unmappedSource.reason: Grammatical-person difference: pinned N1904 ἡμῶν and the pinned TR both say of us, first-person plural; LSV prints of you, second person. The unlike recipients are not equated.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Person difference in the installed translation: LSV of you is second person, whereas both pinned N1904 and TR have ἡμῶν, of us. No source second-person pronoun is invented.

4:8.sourceText: διὸ λέγει Ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν, ἔδωκεν δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
4:8.targetText: for this reason, it says, “Having gone up on high He led captive captivity, and gave gifts to men.”

groups.note: The directional height phrase εἰς ὕψος is rendered on high as the destination/result of ascending, not a claim that εἰς always means on.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective addition: LSV and before gave follows additional TR καί; N1904 directly has ἔδωκεν after captivity.

4:9.sourceText: τὸ δὲ Ἀνέβη τί ἐστιν εἰ μὴ ὅτι καὶ κατέβη εἰς τὰ κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς;
4:9.targetText: And that, He went up, what is it except that He also went down first into the lower parts of the earth?

groups.note: The nominalizing article τὸ introduces the quoted He went up saying; LSV renders this mention of the saying as that, rather than a separate Greek that conjunction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness time addition: LSV first follows additional TR πρῶτον, absent from N1904.

4:10.sourceText: ὁ καταβὰς αὐτός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα.
4:10.targetText: He who went down is the same who also went up far above all the heavens, that He may fill all things—

groups.note: The intensive/identical pronoun αὐτός identifies the descender as the very same person as the ascender; LSV expresses that identification as the same.

4:11.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς ἔδωκεν τοὺς μὲν ἀποστόλους, τοὺς δὲ προφήτας, τοὺς δὲ εὐαγγελιστάς, τοὺς δὲ ποιμένας καὶ διδασκάλους,
4:11.targetText: and He gave some [as] apostles, and some [as] prophets, and some [as] proclaimers of good news, and some [as] shepherds and teachers,

groups.note: The contrastive article/μέν expression begins the distribution some ... others; LSV expresses this first distributive group as some.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English as marks the role in which the given people serve; N1904 gives article/noun role expressions without a separate as conjunction.

4:12.sourceText: πρὸς τὸν καταρτισμὸν τῶν ἁγίων εἰς ἔργον διακονίας, εἰς οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
4:12.targetText: to the perfecting of the holy ones, for a work of ministry, for a building up of the body of the Christ,

4:13.sourceText: μέχρι καταντήσωμεν οἱ πάντες εἰς τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, εἰς ἄνδρα τέλειον, εἰς μέτρον ἡλικίας τοῦ πληρώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
4:13.targetText: until we may all come to the unity of faith and of the recognition of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to a measure of stature of the fullness of the Christ,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article with all supplies the substantive all-of-us description; English has no separate article in we may all come.

4:14.sourceText: ἵνα μηκέτι ὦμεν νήπιοι, κλυδωνιζόμενοι καὶ περιφερόμενοι παντὶ ἀνέμῳ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἐν τῇ κυβίᾳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν πανουργίᾳ πρὸς τὴν μεθοδίαν τῆς πλάνης,
4:14.targetText: that we may no longer be children, being tossed by waves and being carried around by every wind of the teaching, in the cunning of men, in craftiness, to the scheming of leading astray,

groups.note: The wave-tossing verb κλυδωνίζομαι describes being tossed by waves; LSV expresses that lexical wave component explicitly without a separate Greek wave noun.
The instrumental dative every-wind phrase is rendered by every wind, retaining its role as the force carrying people around.

4:15.sourceText: ἀληθεύοντες δὲ ἐν ἀγάπῃ αὐξήσωμεν εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα, ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλή, Χριστός,
4:15.targetText: and [speaking] truth in love, we may increase to Him [in] all things, who is the head—the Christ;

groups.note: The verb ἀληθεύω means being truthful/acting or speaking truth. LSV makes its interpreted speech sense explicit in brackets, [speaking] truth; the full actual truthing verb supports that phrase, without inventing a separate λέγω verb.

The adverbial accusative τὰ πάντα expresses in all respects/things; LSV marks the English relation word in in brackets. The complete case-marked expression supports [in] all things without a separately printed Greek ἐν.

4:16.sourceText: ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα συναρμολογούμενον καὶ συνβιβαζόμενον διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας κατ’ ἐνέργειαν ἐν μέτρῳ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου μέρους τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ σώματος ποιεῖται εἰς οἰκοδομὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ.
4:16.targetText: from whom the whole body, being fitly joined together and united, through the supply of every joint, according to the working in the measure of each single part, the increase of the body makes for the building up of itself in love.

review.note: Greek has through every joint of the supply, while LSV reorders the dependent nouns as through the supply of every joint. Their actual joint/supply nouns and quantifier remain separate precise heads, with the altered genitive attachment explicit; the body remains the subject of makes despite the fronted increase-of-the-body phrase.

4:17.sourceText: Τοῦτο οὖν λέγω καὶ μαρτύρομαι ἐν Κυρίῳ, μηκέτι ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καθὼς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη περιπατεῖ ἐν ματαιότητι τοῦ νοὸς αὐτῶν,
4:17.targetText: This, then, I say, and I testify in the LORD: you are no longer to walk, as also the other nations walk, in the vanity of their mind,

groups.note: The infinitive περιπατεῖν gives the prescribed conduct after I say/testify; English recasts it as are ... to walk. The English are is part of that prescriptive infinitival construction, not a source copula assigned to the article.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness designation addition: LSV other nations follows additional TR λοιπά, absent from N1904.

4:18.sourceText: ἐσκοτωμένοι τῇ διανοίᾳ ὄντες, ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ, διὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν τὴν οὖσαν ἐν αὐτοῖς, διὰ τὴν πώρωσιν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν,
4:18.targetText: being darkened in the understanding, being alienated from the life of God, because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardness of their heart,

groups.note: The dative understanding phrase expresses the respect/sphere of darkening, rendered in the understanding.
The genitive life phrase complements alienated; LSV expresses that complement relation as from the life without an independently printed Greek from preposition.

4:19.sourceText: οἵτινες ἀπηλγηκότες ἑαυτοὺς παρέδωκαν τῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσης ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ.
4:19.targetText: who, having ceased to feel, gave themselves up to the licentiousness, for the working of all uncleanness in greediness;

groups.note: The perfect participle ἀπηλγηκότες describes having become callous/past moral feeling in this conduct context, rendered having ceased to feel; it does not assert a physical anesthesia diagnosis.

4:20.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως ἐμάθετε τὸν Χριστόν,
4:20.targetText: and you did not so learn the Christ,

4:21.sourceText: εἴ γε αὐτὸν ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐδιδάχθητε, καθώς ἐστιν ἀλήθεια ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ,
4:21.targetText: if [it] so be [that] you heard Him, and were taught in Him, as truth is in Jesus;

groups.note: εἴ γε means if indeed; LSV uses the older conditional idiom if [it] so be [that]. The whole conditional expression supports if/so be, without pretending that γε by itself is a Greek be verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English subject supports the idiom if it so be; Greek has the conditional/affirmative particles εἴ γε without a separate it pronoun.
Bracketed English complementizer completes if it so be that; Greek directly continues with you heard Him.

4:22.sourceText: ἀποθέσθαι ὑμᾶς κατὰ τὴν προτέραν ἀναστροφὴν τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης,
4:22.targetText: concerning the former behavior you are to put off the old man, that is corrupt according to the desires of the deceit,

groups.note: The putting-off infinitive ἀποθέσθαι is rendered as the prescribed are to put off construction; its accusative subject ὑμᾶς remains the English you.

The present passive corruption participle φθειρόμενον is rendered is corrupt in a relative clause. The English finite auxiliary belongs to that participle-to-finite recast, while the article stays with that only.

4:23.sourceText: ἀνανεοῦσθαι δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν,
4:23.targetText: and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind,

groups.note: The dative spirit phrase marks the sphere/respect of renewal, rendered in the spirit without a separately printed Greek ἐν.

4:24.sourceText: καὶ ἐνδύσασθαι τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ Θεὸν κτισθέντα ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ὁσιότητι τῆς ἀληθείας.
4:24.targetText: and to put on the new man, which, according to God, was created in righteousness and kindness of the truth.

groups.note: LSV kindness is the unusual historical rendering also printed by Young’s Literal Translation for ὁσιότης. The actual Greek head means piety/holiness or fidelity to holy obligations (Thayer, Strong3742), not the ordinary kindness noun χρηστότης. This exact translation correspondence exposes that Greek head and preserves the interpretive difference rather than teaching a general piety = benevolence synonym.

4:25.sourceText: Διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων μέλη.
4:25.targetText: For this reason, putting away the lying, each speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:26.sourceText: ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε· ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐπιδυέτω ἐπὶ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν,
4:26.targetText: be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your wrath,

4:27.targetText: neither give place to the Devil;

4:28.sourceText: ὁ κλέπτων μηκέτι κλεπτέτω, μᾶλλον δὲ κοπιάτω ἐργαζόμενος ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσὶν τὸ ἀγαθόν, ἵνα ἔχῃ μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι.
4:28.targetText: whoever is stealing let him no longer steal, but rather let him labor, working the thing that is good with the hands, that he may have to impart to him having need.

groups.note: The instrumental dative article/hands noun phrase is rendered with the hands; the intervening source own adjective is separately explained as unrepresented.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness modifier difference: N1904 explicitly has own, ἰδίαις, with hands; LSV/TR has the hands without that adjective.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula in the thing that is good is supplied for the substantival adjective τὸ ἀγαθόν; Greek has no finite be verb or being participle in that nominal phrase. The earlier is belongs to the actual stealing participle.

4:29.sourceText: πᾶς λόγος σαπρὸς ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκπορευέσθω, ἀλλὰ εἴ τις ἀγαθὸς πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας, ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν.
4:29.targetText: Let no corrupt word go forth out of your mouth, but what is good to the necessary building up, that it may give grace to the hearers;

groups.note: The universal word expression with μή, every corrupt word is not to go out, is rendered Let no corrupt word go forth. The universal and negative share the English no through that scope recast.

The conditional-indefinite εἴ τις, if any [word], is rendered as the free-relative what in but what is good. The whole conditional designation is linked without assigning an interrogative meaning to a bare if particle.
The genitive need phrase τῆς χρείας qualifying building up becomes English adjective necessary; the underlying need noun is retained in that complete modifier constituent.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English is supplies the verbless good-word condition εἴ τις ἀγαθός, if any [word is] good; N1904 has no finite be verb or being participle in that clause.

4:30.sourceText: καὶ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως.
4:30.targetText: and do not make the Holy Spirit of God sorrowful, in which you were sealed to [the] day of redemption.

groups.note: The causative grief verb λυπεῖτε means grieve/make sorrowful; English separates its cause and state as make ... sorrowful around the actual Spirit object.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated attributive article before Holy has no separate English word in the preposed Holy-Spirit phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English definite article supplies the specific day designation; Greek ἡμέραν is anarthrous here.

4:31.sourceText: πᾶσα πικρία καὶ θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ καὶ κραυγὴ καὶ βλασφημία ἀρθήτω ἀφ’ ὑμῶν σὺν πάσῃ κακίᾳ.
4:31.targetText: Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamor, and slander, be put away from you, with all malice,

4:32.sourceText: γίνεσθε δὲ εἰς ἀλλήλους χρηστοί, εὔσπλαγχνοι, χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς καθὼς καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἐν Χριστῷ ἐχαρίσατο ὑμῖν.
4:32.targetText: and become kind to one another, tender-hearted, forgiving one another, according as God also forgave you in Christ.

groups.note: The plural reflexive ἑαυτοῖς is used reciprocally with forgiving, yourselves/each other; LSV renders one another for those same second-person recipients, not a different person. The earlier one another has its own actual ἀλλήλους token.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
